title: On the Performance of Volatility-Managed Portfolios
one_line: Across 103 equity strategies, volatility-managed versions show in-sample alphas but do NOT beat the unmanaged originals in real time: out of sample they earn lower Sharpe ratios and certainty-equivalent returns (only momentum, ROE and BAB avoid significant degradation) because the scaling coefficients are unstable.

findings.statement: Real-time: volatility management generally lowers Sharpe vs the original strategy, market factor included.
Robust to window length, rolling samples and leverage limits.

why.pattern: In-sample spanning regressions overstate the benefit of scaling by inverse variance.

reported_results.headline: Across 103 equity strategies, volatility-managed versions show in-sample alphas but do NOT beat the unmanaged originals in real time: out of sample they earn lower Sharpe ratios and certainty-equivalent returns (only momentum, ROE and BAB avoid significant degradation) because the scaling coefficients are unstable.

tradable_edge: No new strategy. Confirms our rule: volatility sizing is a sizing VIEW, not a source of edge — judge strategies at 1 contract first.
data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 5, 2026-11-10), not by the weekly pipeline.
